children: Revenue from operations rises 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore as 5G subscribers cross 300 million and fixed broadband base reaches 30 million

Jio Platforms has delivered double-digit growth in profit and revenue in its first quarterly results since its stock market listing, with consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rising 13.7 per cent year on year to Rs 8,387 crore in Q2 FY27. The company, which raised Rs 30,188 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), reported its results two days after its shares began trading on the stock exchanges on 28 October.

Revenue from operations increased 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore in the September quarter, against Rs 36,332 crore in the corresponding period last year. The figure was also 3.3 per cent higher than the Rs 39,173 crore recorded in Q1 FY27.

Profit after tax increased 8 per cent sequentially from Rs 7,764 crore in the June quarter. Gross revenue, which includes revenue beyond operations, stood at Rs 47,485 crore, up 11.3 per cent year on year from Rs 42,652 crore and 3.3 per cent quarter on quarter from Rs 45,961 crore.

The earnings growth came alongside an improvement in operating margins. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 16.6 per cent year on year to Rs 21,879 crore from Rs 18,757 crore. On a sequential basis, Ebitda increased 4.9 per cent from Rs 20,865 crore.

Ebitda margin expanded to 54.1 per cent from 51.6 per cent a year earlier, a gain of 250 basis points. The margin was 53.3 per cent in the preceding quarter. Jio Platforms attributed the improvement to revenue growth, operating leverage and a stronger margin profile.
Earnings And Cash Generation
Profit before tax (PBT) increased 13.3 per cent year on year to Rs 11,259 crore from Rs 9,937 crore. The figure was 8 per cent higher than the Rs 10,427 crore reported in Q1 FY27.
Earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) grew 18.1 per cent to Rs 14,268 crore from Rs 12,082 crore in Q2 FY26. Its margin rose 200 basis points year on year to 35.3 per cent.

For the six months ended September 2026, revenue from operations reached Rs 79,648 crore, against Rs 71,364 crore in the corresponding period last year, an increase of 11.6 per cent. PAT rose 11.5 per cent to Rs 16,151 crore from Rs 14,485 crore, while Ebitda increased 15.9 per cent to Rs 42,744 crore from Rs 36,892 crore.

Cash generation also improved. Ebitda less cash capital expenditure stood at Rs 32,130 crore in the first half of FY27, nearly double the Rs 16,216 crore reported in the year-ago period. The company defines cash capital expenditure as cash outflow on property, plant and equipment, spectrum and other intangible assets, net of disposal proceeds.
5G And Broadband Expansion

Jio Platforms' customer base reached 542.4 million at the end of September, compared with 506.4 million a year earlier. The company added 9.1 million customers during the quarter, against 8.3 million in Q2 FY26. Monthly churn declined to 1.6 per cent from 1.9 per cent in the year-ago quarter.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) increased 3.5 per cent year on year to Rs 218.8 from Rs 211.4. It also rose from Rs 215.6 in Q1 FY27. The company said promotional offers for fixed broadband customers partly offset the benefits of a better subscriber mix and higher usage.
The 5G subscriber base crossed 300 million in September, with 66 million additions over the preceding 12 months. The technology accounted for around 56 per cent of Jio's total wireless traffic.

The fixed broadband base reached 30 million subscribers, following the addition of 7.3 million connections over the past year. Jio AirFiber accounted for 15.1 million of these subscribers and contributed more than 75 per cent of fixed broadband additions during the period.

Data consumption continued to rise alongside subscriber growth. Total data traffic increased 22.1 per cent year on year to 71.3 billion GB in Q2 FY27. Monthly data consumption per customer reached 44.2 GB, compared with 38.7 GB in the corresponding quarter last year.
IPO Proceeds And Debt

Jio Platforms' market debut on 28 October marked its entry into the listed market. The IPO, which comprised a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares at Rs 1,119 apiece, generated gross proceeds of Rs 30,188 crore after the employee discount.

The company has allocated a substantial portion of the net proceeds towards reducing borrowings at its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Jio Platforms said Rs 27,500 crore had been used to repay, either fully or partly, the principal outstanding on certain external commercial borrowings. The remaining proceeds will go towards general corporate purposes, in accordance with the IPO prospectus.

The company is also positioning its digital services portfolio around emerging technologies. At India Mobile Congress 2026, it showcased Jio Call Agent, an artificial intelligence-based tool that can transcribe and summarise calls, and JioFrames, a smart camera product with voice assistance, live translation and other connected features.

Jio Platforms Managing Director Akash M Ambani said the latest results reflected the expansion of the company's 5G network and broadband and digital services. He also identified satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and artificial intelligence integration across voice and data services as areas for future investment.
